scope: A precise counterexample to unrestricted smooth recovery of relative non-pluripolar adjoints. On P1 x P1 an admissible unbounded ordinary model type has singleton support dV and the meaningful residual adjoint beta/4. Two monotone, uniformly positive smooth regularizations converge canonically, in capacity and smoothly off the pole divisor, with log-densities converging in all finite Lp, but have different normalized classical adjoint probability limits, each placing mass one half on the divisor. Fixed-type, mass-preserving or uniformly integrable-exponential extensions are not refuted; broader S07 remains open.

exact_task.problem: Let X be a connected compact complex n-fold, n>=2, with a smooth positive probability volume dV and dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. All potentials are genuine canonical upper representatives. For a smooth semipositive big real (1,1) background theta, define P_theta(f) as the usc envelope of genuine theta-psh v<=f (equivalently the a.e. obstacle convention with canonical regularization). Put u preceq phi when u<=phi+C, and u~phi for mutual bounded difference including common poles. Define P_theta[phi]=(lim_{C->infinity}P_theta(min(phi+C,0)))^*. An ordinary model reference is sup phi=0 and P_theta[phi]=phi. The standard admissible reference regime additionally requires a genuine envelope P_(epsilon theta)(phi) for some 0<epsilon<1. Then each bounded logarithmic density F has an ordinary-type solution MA_ext_theta(u)=c_phi(F)exp(F)dV with u~phi and scalar c_phi(F)>0 uniquely determined; potential uniqueness is not automatic. Set B_phi(F)=log c_phi(F). For F continuous define A_phi(F) as all Borel probabilities nu such that B_phi(G)<=B_phi(F)-integral(G-F)dnu for every G continuous. In the admissible regime B_phi is concave, decreasing, 1-Lipschitz, and B_phi(F+a)=B_phi(F)-a; A_phi(F) is nonempty compact convex and absolutely continuous with respect to dV. Generic singleton supports hold on a dense G_delta. The same bounded-type functional exists for arbitrary Hermitian theta and phi=0. Smooth strictly positive solution forms Omega=theta+dd^c u have the classical adjoint: a positive smooth weight rho with dd^c(rho Omega^(n-1))=0 and nu=rho Omega^n/integral rho Omega^n. Extended products for rough potentials are non-pluripolar products with the smooth-background corrections; a weighted product is not declared defined merely because a supporting probability exists. Original S07 asks, in singular-reference and degenerate-background admissible regimes, for hypotheses giving a singleton A_phi(F) and an approximation-independent adjoint of a meaningful weak linearized Monge-Ampere operator. Specify a product and a weight rho for dd^c(rho(theta+dd^c u)^(n-1))=0, its normalization and relation to the supporting probability, and prove independence of admissible approximation. If every smooth positive potential perturbation is Gauduchon, normalized Monge-Ampere measures already extend bounded adjoints and are continuous under bounded capacity convergence, including Gauduchon surfaces; repeating these cases is insufficient. Supporting probabilities and their weak stability already exist without defining the displayed product. Smooth-density singleton supports in the Hermitian zero-reference regime do not settle singular references, degenerate residuals or arbitrary unbounded potentials. Control of potentials alone does not control conformal multipliers. No candidate hypothesis, weak product, weight or proof is supplied.

notes.text:
This note constructs and checks a genuine singular-reference target used in the approximation obstruction in n2. All constants use dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂.

1. Geometry and singular potential.
Let X=P1×P1. Let ω1 and ω2 be the pullbacks of the Fubini–Study form, each normalized to integral 1 on its factor. Put
  dV=ω1∧ω2,   theta=2ω1+2ω2.
Thus dV is a smooth positive probability and theta is Kähler (in particular smooth semipositive and big). Fix p on the first P1. For the section s of O(1) vanishing at p, use its standard Fubini–Study metric, scaled so r=|s|² has maximum 1. Define
  D={p}×P1,   psi=log r,   beta=theta−ω1=ω1+2ω2.
Here psi is the genuine canonical logarithmic representative, equal to −infinity on D. Poincaré–Lelong, with the displayed convention, gives
  dd^c psi=[D]−ω1,
so theta+dd^c psi=beta+[D]. On X\D it is the smooth positive form beta. Directly from the non-pluripolar definition, which excludes D, its extended products are
  <theta+dd^c psi>=beta,   <(theta+dd^c psi)^2>=beta²=4dV.
The smooth form beta and its powers put no mass on D, so these extensions do not introduce any unspecified boundary product.

2. Checking the ordinary model and the extra admissibility hypothesis.
Put phi=P_theta[psi]. We verify phi~psi, rather than assuming preservation of analytic singularities.
For C≥0 set v_C=P_theta(min(psi+C,0)). The obstacle and the competitor psi imply
  psi≤v_C≤0,   v_C≤psi+C.
These inequalities hold for canonical representatives; near D the upper bound tends to −infinity, so usc regularization does not change it. On X\D let w_C=v_C−psi. Then 0≤w_C≤C and beta+dd^c w_C≥0. Since beta is closed, it has local smooth potentials. The usual removable-singularity statement for locally upper-bounded psh functions across a complex hypersurface, applied after adding such a local potential, extends w_C as a bounded beta-psh function on X. This removable statement follows locally by defining the extension by limsup and applying the submean inequality on complex lines; boundedness above prevents a negative boundary defect. In particular no external result about singular envelopes is required.

There is a bound sup_X w_C≤K independent of C. Here are details of the compact estimate used for this claim. Fix ω=ω1+ω2 and its Riemannian Laplacian with the subharmonic sign. The inequality beta+dd^c w≥0 implies Δ_ω w≥−K0, with K0 fixed. A normalized Green kernel G(x,y) for this Laplacian can be chosen nonpositive and with uniformly bounded absolute integral. For a smooth w,
  w(x)−average(w)=∫G(x,y)Δw(y)dy≤K1.
Indeed Δw+K0 is a positive measure and G≤0. The same inequality for bounded quasi-psh w follows by Laplacian heat regularization and canonical limits. Hence, if S=sup w, then ∫(S−w)≤K1 Vol(X). On the fixed positive-volume set E={r≥1/2}, the obstacle v_C≤0 gives w_C≤log2. Therefore
  (S_C−log2)Vol(E)≤∫_E(S_C−w_C)≤K1 Vol(X),
which is the promised uniform bound. It follows that
  psi≤phi≤psi+K.
Also phi≤0 and phi≥psi with sup psi=0, so sup phi=0.

The operator P_theta[·] depends only on bounded-equivalence type: shifting its input by a bounded amount merely shifts the parameter C between two bounded translates, and squeezing the increasing limits proves equality. Since phi~psi, this gives P_theta[phi]=P_theta[psi]=phi. Thus phi is an ordinary model reference.

Take epsilon=3/4. Then
  epsilon theta−ω1=(1/2)ω1+(3/2)ω2>0.
Consequently psi is epsilon theta-psh and psi≤phi. It is a genuine competitor for P_(epsilon theta)(phi). This envelope is not identically −infinity and is bounded above by 0. Thus phi satisfies exactly the additional admissible-reference condition in the question.

3. Scalar functional and singleton supports in this singular class.
If v~phi, then v~psi. On X\D, w=v−psi is bounded and beta-psh. Adding local potentials of beta and using the same removable argument extends it as a bounded beta-psh function on X. The equality v=psi+w holds canonically, including their common poles. Set T=beta+dd^c w. On X\D the extended Monge–Ampère product is T², in the bounded Bedford–Taylor sense.

For completeness one can check specifically that T² does not charge D, without invoking a general theorem about arbitrary pluripolar sets. Shift w by a constant so 0≤w≤M. Define the bounded quasi-psh cutoff
  f_t=max(psi/t,−1),  t>0.
Then dd^c f_t≥−ω1/t, −f_t=1 on D, and f_t→0 on X\D. Bounded Bedford–Taylor integration by parts and closedness of T+beta give
  ∫(−f_t)T²
  =∫(−f_t)beta²+∫w dd^c(−f_t)∧(T+beta)
  ≤∫(−f_t)beta²+(M/t)∫ω1∧(T+beta).
The last mixed mass is finite and independent of w: Stokes gives ∫ω1∧T=∫ω1∧beta=2. The first integral tends to zero by dominated convergence against a smooth volume. Since ∫(−f_t)T²≥T²(D), this proves T²(D)=0. All identities here are bounded-potential identities: they follow from the local definition dd^c(wS) for closed Bedford–Taylor currents and integration by parts, or from bounded regularization followed by that definition. No multiplication of an unbounded function by a measure is used.

The same bounded-current Stokes identity gives
  ∫T²=∫beta²=4;
for example T²−beta²=dd^c(w(T+beta)). Thus MA_ext_theta(v)=T² globally, and its mass is 4 for every v of the reference type.

The task supplies existence of ordinary-type solutions and uniqueness of their scalar for all bounded logarithmic densities in this admissible regime. Integrating their equation therefore yields
  c_phi(G)=4/(∫e^G dV),
  B_phi(G)=log4−log(∫e^G dV).
This use of solvability is exactly a premise of the problem, not an unverified external singular Monge–Ampère theorem.

For continuous F put Z_F=∫e^F dV and nu_F=e^F dV/Z_F. Jensen proves
  log Z_G−log Z_F≥∫(G−F)dnu_F,
so nu_F belongs to A_phi(F). Conversely, if nu belongs to A_phi(F), apply its defining inequality to G=F±th for an arbitrary continuous real h and let t tend to zero. Differentiation under the integral gives ∫h dnu=∫h dnu_F. Therefore
  A_phi(F)={nu_F}.
In particular A_phi(0)={dV}.

4. An explicitly defined adjoint at the singular target.
The potential u=psi is an ordinary-type solution for F=0 with c_phi(0)=4. Its non-pluripolar residual is beta. The first weighted product is, by ordinary smooth multiplication,
  Q=rho <theta+dd^c u>=beta/4,   rho=1/4.
It satisfies dd^c Q=0 and ∫rho <(theta+dd^c u)^2>=1. The associated probability is rho beta²=dV, precisely the singleton support just calculated.
For a smooth test perturbation h, the residual linearization is the measure-valued operator
  L_u h=2dd^c h∧beta.
It is the derivative of the non-pluripolar square for u+th while beta+tdd^c h remains positive. Stokes gives ∫rho L_u h=0. Hence the product, normalization, operator identity and supporting-probability relation are all meaningful at this unbounded potential.

This note does not assert that this adjoint is recovered by arbitrary smooth regularizations of u. The difference between its non-pluripolar residual mass 4 and the smooth theta-class mass 8 is central to n2.

correctness.report:
The construction and both summaries are consistent. PASS is conditional on the classical analytic premises listed below; these are isolated for source validation rather than claimed to have been checked at primary sources here.

Subtracting psi from each obstacle envelope gives a bounded beta-psh remainder. Removable extension and the compact sup-minus-average estimate justify the uniform bound using the positive-volume set {r>=1/2}. Consequently phi~psi, type invariance proves the model identity, and psi is indeed a competitor for the additional epsilon=3/4 envelope.

The bounded-current calculation is valid: dd^c f_t>=-omega1/t, and integration by parts gives the stated upper bound for integral(-f_t)T^2. Since the mixed mass is fixed and the smooth-volume term tends to zero, T^2(D)=0. Stokes gives total mass 4. Thus the task-granted solvability applies and yields exactly c_phi(G)=4/integral exp(G)dV. Jensen and two-sided directional differentiation establish the singleton supporting probability without assuming potential uniqueness.

At u=psi, the non-pluripolar products are the smooth residual beta and beta^2. The weight 1/4 has the claimed normalization, closed weighted current, and annihilation identity for h->2dd^c h wedge beta. Neither summary claims approximation independence, which the note expressly leaves to the obstruction analysis.
premises: Let U be a domain in C^m and H an analytic hypersurface in U. If q is plurisubharmonic on U\H and locally bounded above near H, its extension to H by limsup from U\H is plurisubharmonic on U and is the unique extension with the canonical upper representative. If q is locally bounded both above and below near H, this extension is locally bounded.

On a connected compact Riemannian manifold M without boundary, with Laplacian Delta=div grad and Riemannian volume dmu, there is a Green kernel G satisfying Delta_y G(x,y)=delta_x-1/Vol(M). Its additive constant can be chosen so that G<=0 and sup_x integral_M |G(x,y)|dmu(y)<infinity. For every smooth real f, f(x)-Vol(M)^(-1)integral_M f dmu=integral_M G(x,y)Delta f(y)dmu(y). On a compact Kähler manifold, the positivity-preserving Laplacian heat semigroup commutes with Delta and converges pointwise to the canonical representative of every bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic function; in particular a distributional lower bound Delta f>=-A is preserved by this regularization.

Let X be a compact Kähler surface, alpha a smooth closed Kähler form, and w a bounded canonical alpha-plurisubharmonic function. Put T=alpha+dd^c w and use bounded Bedford–Taylor products. Then T^2 and its mixed products with smooth closed semipositive forms are positive, T^2-alpha^2=dd^c(w(T+alpha)), and integral_X T^2=integral_X alpha^2. For every bounded canonical quasi-plurisubharmonic f, the signed mixed product dd^c f wedge (T+alpha) is defined and integral_X f(T^2-alpha^2)=integral_X w dd^c f wedge (T+alpha). If dd^c f>=-eta for a smooth closed semipositive form eta, this mixed product is bounded below by -eta wedge (T+alpha), and integral_X eta wedge T=integral_X eta wedge alpha.

source.report:
All three supplied premise strings are established, with their stated hypotheses and applications.

Premise 0 follows from [Demailly, Theorem I.5.24](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf). An analytic hypersurface is locally pluripolar, using log|g| for a local defining function. The unique canonical extension equals the stated limsup; local upper and lower bounds persist. This applies to the bounded remainders after adding local potentials of beta.

For premise 1, [Aubin, Theorem 4.13](https://www.kfki.hu/~iracz/sgimp/cikkek/nlinear_Problems_in_Riemannian_Geometry__Springer_Monographs_in_Mathematics_.pdf) uses the opposite Laplacian sign. Negating its kernel gives the supplied representation and distributional equation. Its uniform lower bound and integrable diagonal estimates allow a constant shift making the negated kernel nonpositive with uniformly bounded absolute integrals. [Grigor’yan, Sections 2.2–2.4](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~grigor/noteps.pdf) establishes the positive heat kernel and spectral semigroup. These imply commutation with Delta, preservation of constants and of Delta f >= -A. The pointwise assertion also follows: S_t f+At increases with t, so its limit as t decreases to zero is upper semicontinuous and equals f almost everywhere. Canonical quasi-psh representatives give the lower inequality everywhere; positivity and concentration of the heat kernel, together with upper semicontinuity, give the reverse inequality. Thus the limit is the canonical f at every point. No preservation of plurisubharmonicity by heat flow is required.

For premise 2, bounded products, multilinearity and positivity are established in [Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Section 3.1](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42543-025-00105-2). [BEGZ, Theorem 1.14](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/BEGZ10.pdf), with A empty and the closed positive current Θ=T+alpha, gives the asserted integration-by-parts formula. Multilinearity gives T²-alpha²=dd^c w wedge Θ; testing the formula against smooth functions identifies this with dd^c(wΘ). Stokes yields both mass identities. Locally adding a smooth potential of eta to f proves the stated mixed-product lower bound. The cutoff is bounded quasi-psh, and its negative is handled by linearity, so the note’s use is valid.

The geometric constants, admissibility check, divisor cutoff, scalar integration and support differentiation are consistent with these results and the task-granted solvability. Approval preserves the note’s restricted conclusion: the explicit singular target and its adjoint are verified; recovery by arbitrary smooth approximations is not asserted or established.

D={p}×P¹,  ψ=log r,  β=θ−ω₁=ω₁+2ω₂.
The canonical value of ψ on D is −∞. Then
θ+dd^cψ=β+[D],
⟨θ+dd^cψ⟩=β,
⟨(θ+dd^cψ)²⟩=β²=4dV.
In particular these non-pluripolar products have no mass on D, although the current θ+dd^cψ has a divisorial component.

P_θ[q]=(lim_{C→∞}P_θ(min(q+C,0)))^*.

ψ≤φ≤ψ+K,  φ≤0.

εθ−ω₁=(1/2)ω₁+(3/2)ω₂>0,
ψ is εθ-psh and ψ≤φ, and P_{εθ}(φ) is a genuine envelope, not identically −∞ and bounded above by 0. Hence φ satisfies the additional admissible-reference condition in the question.

For every genuine θ-psh v∼φ, the function v−ψ on X\D has a unique canonical extension w to a bounded β-psh function on X, and v=ψ+w canonically, including the common poles on D. Put T=β+dd^cw and use bounded Bedford–Taylor products for T. Then
T²(D)=0,
MA_ext,θ(v)=T²,
∫_X T²=∫_Xβ²=4.

Under the ordinary-type solvability and uniqueness of the positive scalar stipulated in the question, for every bounded real logarithmic density G, the scalar in
MA_ext,θ(v)=c_φ(G)e^GdV,  v∼φ,
is
c_φ(G)=4/(∫_X e^GdV),
and consequently
B_φ(G)=log c_φ(G)=log 4−log(∫_X e^GdV).
For every continuous real F, define A_φ(F) to be the Borel probabilities ν satisfying
B_φ(G)≤B_φ(F)−∫_X(G−F)dν
for every continuous real G. Then
A_φ(F)={ν_F},  ν_F=e^FdV/(∫_X e^FdV).
In particular A_φ(0)={dV}. No uniqueness of the solution potential is assumed in these scalar and support conclusions.

The genuinely unbounded potential u=ψ is an ordinary-type solution at the smooth density F=0, with c_φ(0)=4. Its normalized weak adjoint is given by the positive smooth constant weight ρ=1/4 and the explicitly defined product
Q=ρ⟨θ+dd^cu⟩=β/4,
where multiplication is ordinary multiplication of the smooth residual form β. It satisfies
 dd^cQ=0,
 ∫_Xρ⟨(θ+dd^cu)²⟩=1,
 ρ⟨(θ+dd^cu)²⟩=dV,
so its probability is exactly the singleton element of A_φ(0).
For every h∈C^∞(X,ℝ) and every real t for which β+tdd^ch remains strictly positive,
MA_ext,θ(u+th)=(β+tdd^ch)².

L_uh=(d/dt)|_{t=0}MA_ext,θ(u+th)=2dd^ch∧β,

reconstruction.proof:
Write ω=ω₁+ω₂. All three forms ω, θ and β are closed Kähler forms; ωᵢ²=0, ∫X dV=1, β²=4dV, and θ²=8dV. We use bounded Bedford–Taylor products only for bounded residual potentials.

1. The divisor and removable residuals. With the specified dd^c convention, the Poincaré–Lelong formula for the Fubini–Study metric gives dd^c log r=[D]−ω₁. Thus θ+dd^cψ=β+[D]. Off D this current is β. Non-pluripolar products discard D, and the smooth forms β and β² give D zero mass. Consequently ⟨θ+dd^cψ⟩=β and ⟨(θ+dd^cψ)²⟩=β²=4dV.

We first record a removable-residual observation, without assuming the assertions about φ. Suppose a genuine θ-psh v satisfies ψ−M≤v≤ψ+M. On X\D, w=v−ψ is bounded and β-psh. Locally choose a smooth potential b for β. Then w+b is psh off the analytic hypersurface D and is locally bounded above and below. The first supplied premise extends it uniquely as a bounded canonical psh function. These local extensions agree, giving a bounded canonical β-psh function w on X. The equality v=ψ+w holds off D, and both sides have canonical value −∞ on D, so it holds everywhere. This also proves uniqueness of the canonical residual extension.

2. A uniform bound for envelope competitors. Fix the Kähler metric associated with ω, and let averages be taken with its normalized volume, which is dV. There is a constant A≥0, independent of w, such that every bounded β-psh w satisfies Δw≥−A distributionally. Indeed, this follows by tracing dd^cw≥−β against the fixed metric.

Apply the second supplied premise to the heat regularizations w_t. They are smooth, have the same average as w, satisfy Δw_t≥−A, and converge pointwise to the canonical w. If G is the nonpositive Green kernel and M_G=sup_x∫|G(x,y)|dμ(y), its representation gives
w_t(x)−average(w)=∫G(x,y)(Δw_t(y)+A)dμ(y)−A∫G(x,y)dμ(y)≤A M_G.
Passing to the stipulated pointwise limit gives w≤average(w)+A M_G. All hypotheses here hold: X is compact connected Kähler and w is a bounded canonical quasi-psh function.

For C≥0, consider a competitor v≤min(ψ+C,0). Replacing it by max(v,ψ) preserves both constraints and can only increase it. For the replacement, the removable-residual observation gives v=ψ+w, with 0≤w≤C. Moreover v≤0 implies w≤−ψ off D. Since ψ has logarithmic singularities, L:=∫X(−ψ)dV is finite. Hence average(w)≤L, and w≤K:=L+A M_G. It follows that every competitor, and then its canonical envelope, is bounded above by ψ+K, independently of C. The envelope is also at least ψ and at most 0. The upper bound extends across D under usc regularization because ψ+K tends to −∞ there.

Let V(q) denote all genuine θ-psh v≤0 satisfying v≤q+C for some constant C. For q=ψ, the definition of Pθ[ψ] is exactly the canonical usc supremum of V(ψ): each inner envelope is still below its usc obstacle and belongs to this family. The family is locally bounded above by 0 and contains ψ. The elementary local psh upper-envelope construction therefore yields a genuine θ-psh φ, and the preceding bounds give ψ≤φ≤ψ+K and φ≤0.

Since φ∼ψ, V(φ)=V(ψ). Taking their canonical supremum proves Pθ[φ]=φ. To check normalization, let m=supXφ≤0. If m<0, then φ−m belongs to V(ψ), since it is at most 0 and has bounded difference from ψ. The supremum defining φ would give φ−m≤φ, a contradiction. Thus supXφ=0, and φ is an ordinary model reference.

For ε=3/4, εθ+dd^cψ=(1/2)ω₁+(3/2)ω₂+[D] is positive. Thus ψ is a genuine εθ-psh competitor below φ. The envelope P_{εθ}(φ) lies between ψ and φ≤0. The same locally bounded-above envelope construction makes it a genuine εθ-psh function, not identically −∞. This proves the additional admissibility condition.

3. Products and their mass. We give an integration estimate also useful for the declared dependent note. Let α be any closed Kähler form on this surface, let w be bounded canonical α-psh, and put T=α+dd^cw. After adding a constant, assume 0≤w≤M. Set f_k=max(ψ,−k), k>0. These are bounded canonical quasi-psh functions satisfying dd^cf_k≥−ω₁, because both ψ and the constant −k are ω₁-psh.

The third supplied premise applies: α is closed Kähler, w and f_k have exactly its boundedness and canonical-representative hypotheses, and η=ω₁ is smooth closed semipositive. Its integration-by-parts identity and mixed-product lower bound give
∫X f_k(T²−α²)=∫X w dd^cf_k∧(T+α)≥−M∫X ω₁∧(T+α)=−2M∫X ω₁∧α.
Consequently
(E)  ∫X(−f_k)T²≤∫X(−ψ)α²+2M∫X ω₁∧α,
uniformly in k. The right side is finite. Since f_k=−k on D, (E) implies T²(D)=0. It also implies, by monotone convergence, ∫(−ψ)T²<∞. The same supplied premise gives ∫T²=∫α².

Now let v∼φ be any genuine θ-psh function. Since φ∼ψ, the removable-residual observation applies and yields its unique bounded β-psh w. Use α=β in the preceding calculation. Off D, θ+dd^cv=T=β+dd^cw; local bounded Bedford–Taylor products there are its non-pluripolar products. The non-pluripolar product of v gives D no mass by its construction, and we just proved T²(D)=0. Hence the global products agree. Since θ is closed, the extended smooth-background convention here is the usual non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère product. We obtain MA_ext,θ(v)=T² and ∫X MA_ext,θ(v)=∫Xβ²=4.

4. Scalars and supports. Use precisely the ordinary-type solvability stipulated in the question, now applicable because φ is admissible. For any bounded real G, a solution v∼φ satisfies T²=cφ(G)e^GdV. Integrating the equality just proved yields
cφ(G)=4/Z_G,  Z_G:=∫X e^GdV,
and Bφ(G)=log 4−log Z_G. Here 0<Z_G<∞. No uniqueness of v was used.

For continuous F, put ν_F=e^FdV/Z_F. Jensen's inequality gives log(Z_G/Z_F)=log∫e^{G−F}dν_F≥∫(G−F)dν_F. Thus ν_F satisfies every defining supporting inequality. Conversely, if ν belongs to Aφ(F), take G=F+tH, with H continuous and t of either sign. Differentiating the explicit scalar formula at t=0 gives dBφ(F+tH)/dt|₀=−∫H dν_F. The two one-sided supporting inequalities force ∫H dν=∫H dν_F. Continuous tests determine Borel probabilities on compact X, so ν=ν_F. This proves Aφ(F)={ν_F}, in particular Aφ(0)={dV}.

5. The specified singular adjoint. The canonical u=ψ is unbounded, has singularity type φ, and satisfies MA_ext,θ(u)=4dV, so it solves the equation at F=0 with cφ(0)=4. Define ρ=1/4 and define its weighted degree-one non-pluripolar product by ordinary multiplication of its smooth residual:
Q=ρ⟨θ+dd^cu⟩=β/4.
This definition involves neither a multiplier extracted from a supporting measure nor multiplication of a function by an unspecified rough current. Since β is closed, dd^cQ=0. Also ρ⟨(θ+dd^cu)²⟩=dV and its integral is 1. Its probability is exactly the singleton support just established.

For smooth real h and every real t with β+tdd^ch strictly positive, u+th has the same logarithmic divisor and smooth positive residual β+tdd^ch. Removing D therefore gives MA_ext,θ(u+th)=(β+tdd^ch)². Differentiating at zero yields the measure-valued residual linearization L_u h=2dd^ch∧β. Stokes' theorem gives ∫Xρ L_u h=(1/2)∫Xdd^ch∧β=0. Thus Q is a fully specified normalized weak adjoint for this residual operator. These conclusions are confined to this singular potential and residual product; no recovery from arbitrary smooth regularizations is asserted.

notes.summary: Complete obstruction to unrestricted smooth-approximation adjoints in the admissible singular regime. On the target in n1, smooth uniformly theta-positive u_delta^g=log(r+delta e^g) decrease canonically to the same unbounded solution and converge in capacity, C∞ off D, and L1; their smooth logarithmic densities converge to F=0 in every finite Lp. Nevertheless their normalized classical adjoint probabilities have g-dependent limits: (1/2)dV+(1/2)[D]∧ω2+(1/8)[D]∧dd^c g. None equals the singleton support dV. The normalized adjoint currents converge to (beta+[D])/8, not beta/4, and cannot be a function times the non-pluripolar residual beta. No claim is made against fixed-type or uniformly bounded-density approximations.
notes.detailedSummary: The explicitly formulated assertion refuted is: for an admissible singular-reference solution, arbitrary smooth strictly theta-psh regularizations converging canonically and in capacity should yield an approximation-independent normalized classical adjoint, whose probability is the singleton support and whose current is a weighted non-pluripolar residual. It remains false even if one additionally assumes uniform lower positivity, C∞ convergence away from the poles, and convergence of smooth logarithmic densities in all finite Lp. On P1×P1 use n1's theta=2ω1+2ω2, D, r, psi, beta, F=0 and c=4. For any fixed smooth g on the second factor with dd^c g≥−ω2, set u_delta^g=log(r+delta e^g). Writing lambda=r/(r+delta e^g) and h=log r−g−log delta, the exact formula is Omega_delta=(2−lambda)ω1+2ω2+(1−lambda)dd^c g+lambda(1−lambda)dh∧d^c h≥ω1+ω2. Each form is Kähler and has mass 8, so its normalized adjoint weight is the constant 1/8. The normal-spike measure lambda(1−lambda)dlog r∧d^c log r concentrates on D, with lambda asymptotically uniform on [0,1]; averaging the extra factor 1−lambda gives 1/2. Consequently Omega_delta² converges to 4dV+4[D]∧ω2+[D]∧dd^c g. Choosing g=0 and a small nonconstant g gives different limits despite the same limiting canonical potential. The currents (1/8)Omega_delta converge to (beta+[D])/8, containing a divisorial part impossible for any locally integrable multiplier of smooth beta. The density F_delta=log(Omega_delta²/(4dV)) is smooth, satisfies the exact equation with scalar 4, and converges to zero in finite Lp, but ∫e^{F_delta}=2 for every delta. Thus exponentiated densities are not uniformly integrable. The obstruction is mass concentration at poles and loss of non-pluripolar mass, not a failure of conformal-multiplier estimates. Uniform L∞ logarithmic-density or fixed singularity-type/mass-preserving approximation theorems are explicitly outside its scope.
notes.text:
VERIFIED OBSTRUCTION; this is a complete resolution through the obstruction alternative in the task, not an unrestricted existence theorem.

A. The unrestricted assertion being tested.
Consider the following proposed extension of the smooth adjoint construction:
(U) Let theta and phi be in the problem's admissible singular-reference regime. Let u be an ordinary-type solution at a smooth logarithmic density F, and suppose A_phi(F) is singleton. Whenever smooth potentials u_j with smooth strictly positive forms Omega_j=theta+dd^c u_j converge canonically to u, in capacity and smoothly off its pole set, the normalized classical adjoint measures and currents
  nu_j=rho_j Omega_j^n,   Q_j=rho_j Omega_j^(n−1),
  dd^c Q_j=0,   ∫rho_j Omega_j^n=1,
should produce an approximation-independent adjoint of u. In particular nu_j should converge to the singleton support, and the limiting current should be a justified weighted non-pluripolar residual rho <(theta+dd^c u)^(n−1)> with the corresponding normalization.

Here the approximations are unrestricted smooth regularizations: no uniform upper bound on their logarithmic densities and no preservation of relative non-pluripolar mass is assumed. We will disprove (U), even with the additional conditions Omega_j≥a fixed Kähler form and convergence of logarithmic densities in every finite Lp. This is not a bounded-potential Gauduchon continuity example: the limiting potential has a genuine logarithmic divisorial pole and the reference is a genuine admissible ordinary model.

B. The singular solution and its support.
Use exactly the example fully checked in n1:
  X=P1×P1,   theta=2ω1+2ω2,   dV=ω1∧ω2,
  D={p}×P1,   r=|s|² with max r=1,   u=psi=log r,
  beta=ω1+2ω2,   theta+dd^c u=beta+[D].
The reference phi=P_theta[psi] is an ordinary model with phi~psi, and P_((3/4)theta)(phi) is genuine. The ordinary-type equation is
  MA_ext_theta(u)=beta²=4dV,
so F=0 and c_phi(0)=4. Moreover
  A_phi(0)={dV}.
The meaningful normalized non-pluripolar adjoint at u is beta/4, with weight rho=1/4 and supporting probability dV. These facts, including the scalar formula for all continuous densities, are established in n1.

C. A family of strictly positive smooth regularizations.
Let g be any fixed smooth real function on the second P1 such that
  gamma:=dd^c g≥−ω2.
In formulas on X, g and gamma are pulled back from that factor. Both g=0 and any sufficiently small nonconstant g satisfy this condition. For delta>0 define the globally smooth potential
  u_delta^g=log(r+delta e^g).
As delta decreases to zero, u_delta^g decreases pointwise to the same genuine canonical u=log r, including the value −infinity on D. On every compact subset of X\D the convergence is C∞. These are actual monotone smooth regularizations, not merely a sequence of measures declared to represent an adjoint.

Define, on X\D,
  alpha=log r,
  lambda=r/(r+delta e^g),
  h=alpha−g−log delta.
Choose d^c=(i/(4π))(bar∂−∂), so dd^c has the required convention and dh∧d^c h is a positive rank-one (1,1) form. The chain rule for log(e^alpha+delta e^g), using dd^c alpha=−ω1 off D, gives the exact identity
  Omega_delta^g=theta+dd^c u_delta^g
  =A_delta+R_delta,
  A_delta=(2−lambda)ω1+2ω2+(1−lambda)gamma,
  R_delta=lambda(1−lambda)dh∧d^c h.
Hence
  A_delta≥ω1+ω2,   R_delta≥0,
so Omega_delta^g≥ω1+ω2 on X\D and, by continuity of the smooth form, on all X. Thus every approximation is uniformly strictly theta-positive. Each form is closed. Smooth Stokes gives
  ∫(Omega_delta^g)^2=∫theta²=8.

Since the forms are Kähler, their classical adjoint weights are constant: dd^c(rho Omega)=dd^c rho∧Omega=0 is the elliptic harmonic equation for rho, whose smooth solutions on this connected compact manifold are constant by the maximum principle. With the required normalization,
  rho_delta^g=1/8,
  nu_delta^g=(Omega_delta^g)^2/8,
  Q_delta^g=Omega_delta^g/8.
This explicitly controls the conformal multipliers; the counterexample does not hide an unproved assertion about their behavior.

D. Exact limiting probabilities and their dependence on g.
We now compute the weak limit. The computation also verifies all normalization constants.
Because R_delta has rank one, R_delta²=0. Thus
  (Omega_delta^g)^2=A_delta²+2A_delta∧R_delta.
The coefficients of A_delta are uniformly bounded. Since lambda→1 off D,
  A_delta² → beta²=4dV
by dominated convergence.

Put Q_N=dalpha∧d^c alpha and Q_T=dg∧d^c g. Because alpha depends only on the first factor and g only on the second, the cross terms in dh∧d^c h vanish when wedged with the diagonal form A_delta. Consequently
  A_delta∧R_delta
  =lambda(1−lambda)Q_N∧(2ω2+(1−lambda)gamma)
   +lambda(1−lambda)(2−lambda)ω1∧Q_T.
The second term tends to zero as a measure: its smooth density is uniformly bounded and tends to zero almost everywhere.

For the normal term, the following elementary concentration identities hold:
  lambda(1−lambda)Q_N ⇀ [D],
  lambda(1−lambda)^2 Q_N ⇀ (1/2)[D].
They are uniform in the second coordinate. Here is a direct verification, so no general theorem about products of unbounded potentials is needed. Near p use the affine coordinate z in which
  r=|z|²/(1+|z|²).
For fixed second coordinate write delta'=delta e^g. After z=sqrt(delta') zeta, the first normal measure converges to
  (i/(2π)) d zeta∧d bar zeta /(1+|zeta|²)^2.
It has total mass 1. Its radial variable y=|zeta|² has measure dy/(1+y)^2, and lambda converges to y/(1+y). Therefore lambda is uniformly distributed on [0,1] with respect to this normal spike, and the extra factor 1−lambda has average 1/2. Outside a fixed neighborhood of p the normal measure is O(delta'); outside a shrinking rescaled disk its tails are bounded by the tail of dy/(1+y)^2. These bounds justify both weak limits for arbitrary smooth test functions. Since delta' lies between two fixed positive multiples of delta, the argument is uniform over the compact second factor.

It follows that
  (Omega_delta^g)^2 ⇀ 4dV+4[D]∧ω2+[D]∧gamma,
and hence
  nu_delta^g ⇀ nu^g
  :=(1/2)dV+(1/2)[D]∧ω2+(1/8)[D]∧dd^c g.
The displayed measure is positive: its divisorial component is [D]∧(4ω2+gamma)/8, and 4ω2+gamma≥3ω2. Its total mass is 1 because ∫gamma=0 on P1. In particular it has mass 1/2 on D.

For g=0 the limit is
  nu^0=(1/2)dV+(1/2)[D]∧ω2.
Choose a sufficiently small smooth nonconstant g. On P1, dd^c g is then not identically zero (a real globally harmonic function would be constant), so nu^g differs from nu^0. Thus two monotone, uniformly strictly positive smooth approximation sequences of precisely the same canonical unbounded solution have different normalized classical adjoint probability limits. Neither limit can be the singleton support dV; both charge D, whereas dV does not.

E. The limiting weighted current is also incompatible with the required product.
The functions u_delta^g converge to psi in L1. For example 0≤u_delta^g−psi≤log(1+delta e^(max g)/r) off D, and logarithmic integrability near the smooth divisor proves L1 convergence. Therefore distributional differentiation gives
  Q_delta^g=Omega_delta^g/8 ⇀ (beta+[D])/8.
This current is independent of g, but it is not the normalized non-pluripolar adjoint beta/4. More fundamentally it cannot equal rho beta for any locally integrable function rho giving ordinary multiplication of this smooth positive form: rho beta has locally integrable coefficients and no divisorial component, while (beta+[D])/8 has a nonzero singular component on D. Thus a weak limit of the classical weighted currents does not automatically define the displayed weighted non-pluripolar product, even when all conformal multipliers are perfectly controlled constants. The top products retain additional, approximation-dependent information, as the two probabilities above demonstrate.

F. Convergence and solvability properties of the approximation class.
Each regularization is a genuine global smooth theta-psh potential with uniformly positive form. It is an explicit classical solution, so there is no hidden solvability hypothesis. Define its smooth logarithmic density by
  F_delta^g=log((Omega_delta^g)^2/(4dV)).
Then exactly
  (Omega_delta^g)^2=4 exp(F_delta^g)dV.
Each F_delta^g is bounded (separately for each delta) and smooth. On X\D it tends to F=0 in C∞.

In fact F_delta^g→0 in Lp(dV) for every finite p. Uniform positivity gives F_delta^g≥−log2. For the upper bound, |dalpha|² with respect to ω1+ω2 is at most C/r, while g and all its derivatives are bounded. Since lambda(1−lambda)≤1/4, the exact formula gives
  Omega_delta^g≤C(1+1/r)(ω1+ω2)
on X\D, uniformly for small delta. It follows that
  |F_delta^g|≤C+2|log r|.
The right side belongs to every finite Lp(dV), and pointwise convergence off D then proves the claim by dominated convergence.

The potentials also converge in the usual compact Kähler capacity. Indeed, for any eta>0,
  {u_delta^g−psi>eta}⊂{r<delta e^(max g)/(e^eta−1)},
apart from D itself. These are shrinking neighborhoods of the pluripolar divisor. Their capacity tends to zero. In this particular setting this last elementary capacity fact can be checked directly: the bounded logarithmic cutoffs max(psi/t,−1) used in n1, tested against the defining bounded omega-psh capacity potentials and integrated by parts, give a uniform bound tending to zero for the capacity of {psi<−t}. Thus the capacity assertion does not posit convergence at noncanonical values on D. If desired one can impose sup-normalization on the smooth potentials; subtracting their suprema, which tend to zero, leaves all forms and conclusions unchanged.

There is an essential missing density condition:
  ∫exp(F_delta^g)dV=8/4=2
for every delta, whereas ∫exp(0)dV=1. Consequently exponentiated densities are not uniformly integrable and do not converge in L1. The smooth measures preserve theta-class mass 8; the target's non-pluripolar mass is only 4. This explicitly locates the obstruction.

G. Scope of the conclusion.
Assertion (U) is false in a completely verified admissible singular-reference example, even though the supporting probability is singleton and the target itself has a well-defined normalized weak non-pluripolar adjoint. It is false for two different admissible smooth-regularization paths, not merely because a particular sequence lacks a subsequential limit. Uniform lower positivity, monotonic canonical convergence, capacity convergence, smooth convergence off the poles, and finite-Lp convergence of logarithmic densities do not repair it.

The construction does NOT refute a restricted theorem whose approximation class preserves the divisorial singularity type, discards the divisorial concentration before normalization, preserves full relative mass, or requires uniform L∞ bounds on the logarithmic densities or uniform integrability of their exponentials. Smooth approximants in this note are necessarily bounded and are not individually of the singular reference type. That distinction is stated, not suppressed: the assertion refuted is precisely the unrestricted use of smooth regularizations of an unbounded ordinary-type potential. Any positive extension must control or prohibit this concentration mechanism. This is beyond the existing bounded Gauduchon continuity result because its failure is entirely at genuine unbounded poles.

Declared dependency: the construction and conclusions of w7-1/n1.

The following unrestricted implication (U) is false. Let X be a connected compact complex n-fold, n≥2, with smooth positive probability volume dV, θ a smooth semipositive big real (1,1) background, and φ a genuine ordinary model reference with sup_Xφ=0, P_θ[φ]=φ, and a genuine envelope P_{εθ}(φ) for some 0<ε<1. Suppose u is a genuine canonical ordinary-type solution
MA_ext,θ(u)=c_φ(F)e^FdV,  u∼φ,

ν_j=ρ_jΩ_j^n,  Q_j=ρ_jΩ_j^{n−1},
with ρ_j positive smooth, dd^cQ_j=0, and ∫_Xρ_jΩ_j^n=1. The proposed consequent of (U) is that these adjoints recover an approximation-independent weak adjoint of u: ν_j converge to the singleton element of A_φ(F), and Q_j converge independently of the approximating sequence to a meaningfully defined weighted non-pluripolar residual
Q=ρ⟨(θ+dd^cu)^{n−1}⟩,
with dd^cQ=0, ∫_Xρ⟨(θ+dd^cu)^n⟩=1, and associated probability ρ⟨(θ+dd^cu)^n⟩ equal to that singleton support. No uniform bound on the logarithmic densities of the approximants and no preservation of relative non-pluripolar mass are assumptions of (U).

A counterexample exists already in dimension 2 with θ Kähler. Use the data of w7-1/n1:
X=P¹×P¹,  dV=ω₁∧ω₂,  θ=2ω₁+2ω₂,
D={p}×P¹,  r=|s|² with max r=1,  u=ψ=log r,
β=ω₁+2ω₂,  φ=P_θ[ψ]∼ψ.
Here φ is an admissible ordinary model reference with ε=3/4,
θ+dd^cu=β+[D],
MA_ext,θ(u)=β²=4dV,
F=0,  c_φ(0)=4,  A_φ(0)={dV}.
The target itself has the meaningful normalized non-pluripolar adjoint weight ρ=1/4, current β/4, and probability dV.

For every fixed g∈C^∞(P¹,ℝ) on the second factor satisfying γ=dd^cg≥−ω₂, pull g and γ back to X and, for δ>0, define
u_δ^g=log(r+δe^g),  Ω_δ^g=θ+dd^cu_δ^g.
(The notation u_δ^g, rather than ν_δ^g, denotes this potential.) Each u_δ^g is globally smooth and each Ω_δ^g is Kähler, with
Ω_δ^g≥ω₁+ω₂,
∫_X(Ω_δ^g)²=∫_Xθ²=8.
As δ↓0, u_δ^g decreases pointwise to the same canonical u=log r, including the value −∞ on D. It converges to u in L¹ and in C^∞ on every compact subset of X\D. It also converges in the usual compact Kähler capacity for ω=ω₁+ω₂; explicitly, for every η>0 the capacity of
D∪{x∈X\D:|u_δ^g(x)−u(x)|>η}
tends to zero. Here one may take
Cap_ω(E)=sup{∫_E(ω+dd^cv)²:v∈PSH(X,ω), −1≤v≤0}.
The suprema of u_δ^g tend to zero, and subtracting those suprema leaves the forms and all stated adjoint limits unchanged.

The unique normalized positive smooth classical adjoint weight for Ω_δ^g is the constant ρ_δ^g=1/8. Thus, with ν denoting probabilities,
ν_δ^g=(Ω_δ^g)²/8,
Q_δ^g=Ω_δ^g/8,
dd^cQ_δ^g=0,
∫_Xρ_δ^g(Ω_δ^g)²=1.
Their weak limits are
(Ω_δ^g)² ⇀ 4dV+4[D]∧ω₂+[D]∧γ,
ν_δ^g ⇀ ν^g=(1/2)dV+(1/2)[D]∧ω₂+(1/8)[D]∧dd^cg,
Q_δ^g ⇀ (β+[D])/8.
The wedges of [D] with smooth forms in these formulas are ordinary current products. The measure ν^g is positive and has total mass 1; its divisorial component is [D]∧(4ω₂+γ)/8 with 4ω₂+γ≥3ω₂. For every such g, ν^g(D)=1/2, so ν^g is not the singleton support dV.

Both g=0 and every sufficiently small smooth nonconstant real g on the second factor satisfy γ≥−ω₂. For any such nonconstant g, dd^cg is not identically zero and ν^g≠ν^0. Consequently two monotone smooth approximation sequences, each uniformly bounded below by the same Kähler form and converging to precisely the same canonical singular solution, have different normalized classical adjoint probability limits. Their conformal multipliers are nevertheless the identical constants 1/8.

The limiting adjoint current (β+[D])/8 is independent of g but is not the normalized target current β/4. There is no locally integrable function ρ for which ordinary multiplication of the smooth form β gives
ρβ=(β+[D])/8.
Thus this weak limit of classical adjoint currents cannot be interpreted as such a function-weighted non-pluripolar residual.

For each δ>0 and each fixed admissible g, define the smooth logarithmic density
F_δ^g=log((Ω_δ^g)²/(4dV)).
It is bounded for each individual δ, and the approximant is an explicit smooth classical solution of
(Ω_δ^g)²=4e^{F_δ^g}dV.
As δ↓0, F_δ^g→0 in C^∞ on compact subsets of X\D and in every finite L^p(dV). For each fixed g there is a constant C_g, independent of sufficiently small δ, such that on X\D
F_δ^g≥−log 2,
|F_δ^g|≤C_g+2|log r|.
Nevertheless
∫_X e^{F_δ^g}dV=2
for every δ, whereas ∫_X e^0dV=1. The exponentiated densities are not uniformly integrable and do not converge to 1 in L¹. The smooth θ-class mass is 8, while the target non-pluripolar mass is 4.

Hence singleton support, uniform lower positivity of the approximating forms, monotone canonical convergence of the potentials, capacity convergence, smooth convergence off the poles, and convergence of logarithmic densities in every finite L^p do not imply (U). The smooth approximants are bounded and are not individually of the singular reference type φ. This obstruction concerns unrestricted smooth regularizations of an unbounded ordinary-type potential; it makes no assertion of failure for approximation classes that preserve the divisorial singularity type, discard divisorial concentration before normalization, preserve full relative mass, require uniform L^∞ bounds on logarithmic densities, or require uniform integrability of their exponentials.
reconstruction.proof:
We use the established construction of w7-1/n1, including estimate (E) proved there. In particular X is a compact Kähler surface, θ is Kähler, φ is an admissible ordinary model reference with ε=3/4, and the canonical u=ψ is an ordinary-type solution at the smooth density F=0. Its non-pluripolar mass is 4, its singleton support is dV, and its explicitly normalized residual adjoint is β/4 with weight 1/4.

1. The smooth approximations and positivity. Let g be a smooth real function on the second P¹ with γ=dd^cg≥−ω₂. Write γ=aω₂, where a is smooth and a≥−1. For δ>0 set q=δe^g and u_δ^g=log(r+q). This is a globally smooth real function, including on D, since r+q is strictly positive.

On X\D define λ=r/(r+q), μ=q/(r+q), and κ=(i/(2π))∂(ψ−g)∧bar∂(ψ−g). The chain rule gives
Ω_δ^g=(2−λ)ω₁+2ω₂+μγ+λμκ.
Here κ is positive and λ+μ=1. Thus Ω_δ^g≥(2−λ)ω₁+(2−μ)ω₂≥ω₁+ω₂. Since Ω_δ^g is smooth, this inequality extends across D. The forms are closed because θ is closed, so they are Kähler. Stokes' theorem gives ∫X(Ω_δ^g)²=∫Xθ²=8.

As δ decreases to zero, the potentials decrease pointwise to the canonical ψ, including −∞ on D. On X\D,
u_δ^g−ψ=log(1+δe^g/r)≥0.
For 0<δ≤1 this difference is bounded above by a constant plus |log r|. The latter is integrable, so dominated convergence proves L¹ convergence. The displayed formulas also give C^∞ convergence on every compact subset of X\D. Moreover supX u_δ^g=log(1+δe^{max g})→0, since r and g depend on different factors. Subtracting these suprema changes neither the forms nor their adjoints or limits.

Here is an explicit verification of capacity convergence, requiring no assertion of capacity continuity for unbounded potentials. Take α=ω=ω₁+ω₂ in estimate (E) of the supporting proof. For any canonical ω-psh v with −1≤v≤0, apply that estimate with residual w=v+1∈[0,1] and T=ω+dd^cv. It gives
∫X(−max(ψ,−k))T²≤C,
where C=∫X(−ψ)ω²+2∫Xω₁∧ω is independent of v and k and is finite. Therefore Cap_ω({r≤e^{−k}})≤C/k. This includes D. For η>0, the set in the note is contained in {r≤C_{g,η}δ}, with C_{g,η}=e^{max g}/(e^η−1). Using k=−log(C_{g,η}δ) for sufficiently small δ proves its capacity tends to zero.

2. The classical weights. For a smooth positive closed form Ω on this connected compact surface, dd^c(ρΩ)=dd^cρ∧Ω. Thus its classical adjoint equation makes ρ harmonic for the Kähler metric Ω. The maximum principle forces any smooth solution to be constant. For Ω=Ω_δ^g, normalization ∫ρΩ²=1 then gives uniquely ρ_δ^g=1/8. Hence
ν_δ^g=(Ω_δ^g)²/8,  Q_δ^g=Ω_δ^g/8,
with dd^cQ_δ^g=0 and the required probability normalization.

3. Direct computation of the measure limits. Choose a first-factor affine coordinate z with p=0. The specified scaling of the Fubini–Study metric gives
r=|z|²/(1+|z|²),  ω₁=(i/(2π))dz∧dbar z/(1+|z|²)².
In particular the radial push-forward of ω₁ by r is Lebesgue measure dr on [0,1], and angular integration has normalized measure darg z/(2π). Also
(i/(2π))∂ψ∧bar∂ψ=Hω₁,  H=(1−r)/r.
Write (i/(2π))∂g∧bar∂g=Kω₂, with K smooth and nonnegative. The form κ has rank one, so κ²=0. Wedges of either ωᵢ with the cross-factor terms of κ vanish. Squaring the formula for Ω therefore gives, on X\D,
(Ω_δ^g)²=2[(2−λ)(2+μa)+λμ((2−λ)K+(2+μa)H)]dV.
The first bracketed term converges to 2, and its contribution to the measure converges to 4dV by bounded convergence. The term involving K is uniformly bounded and tends to zero almost everywhere, so its measure tends to zero. The remaining, potentially concentrating term is
2 q(1−r)/(r+q)² · (2+qa/(r+q)) dV.
For a fixed second-factor point, its first-factor total mass is 4I₀(q)+2aI₁(q), where
I₀(q)=∫₀¹ q(1−r)/(r+q)² dr,
I₁(q)=∫₀¹ q²(1−r)/(r+q)³ dr.
Substituting r=qt and using dominated convergence shows I₀(q)→1 and I₁(q)→1/2. For example their resulting integrands are (1−qt)/(1+t)² and (1−qt)/(1+t)³ on 0≤t≤1/q, bounded respectively by the integrable functions (1+t)^{−2} and (1+t)^{−3}. The convergence is uniform when q ranges between δe^{min g} and δe^{max g}.

These normal measures concentrate at r=0: on every r≥b>0 their densities are O_g(q), and their total masses are uniformly bounded. For any continuous test on X, uniform continuity permits replacing its value in that concentrating part by its value at (p,y). The preceding normal integrals then yield a limit [D]∧(4ω₂+γ). This establishes, by explicit testing,
(Ω_δ^g)² ⇀ 4dV+4[D]∧ω₂+[D]∧γ.
No multiplication of rough currents is being used in this limit; the divisor is wedged only with the indicated smooth forms.

Since u_δ^g→ψ in L¹, distributional differentiation also gives Ω_δ^g⇀θ+dd^cψ=β+[D]. Dividing by 8, the classical adjoint limits are consequently
ν_δ^g ⇀ ν^g=(1/2)dV+(1/2)[D]∧ω₂+(1/8)[D]∧dd^cg,
Q_δ^g ⇀ (β+[D])/8.
The limiting measure is positive: 4ω₂+γ≥3ω₂. Its total mass is (4+4+∫_{P¹}γ)/8=1, because ∫γ=0. Its mass on D is exactly 1/2, whereas dV(D)=0. Thus it is not the singleton support dV.

Taking g=0 gives one such sequence. There are also smooth nonconstant g with γ≥−ω₂: scale any fixed nonconstant smooth real function by a sufficiently small nonzero constant. A nonconstant smooth function on compact P¹ cannot have dd^cg=0, by the maximum principle. Thus for this choice [D]∧dd^cg≠0 and ν^g≠ν^0. Taking, for example, δ_j=2^{−j} supplies two monotone smooth approximation sequences with the required common limit and different adjoint probability limits. Their conformal weights are nevertheless identically the same constants 1/8.

4. Why the limiting current is not a function-weighted residual. The target non-pluripolar degree-one residual is the smooth β. Ordinary multiplication ρβ by any locally integrable function has coefficients absolutely continuous with respect to smooth volume. In contrast, (β+[D])/8 has a nonzero divisorial singular part: its wedge with the smooth ω has positive mass on D. Therefore no such function ρ can satisfy ρβ=(β+[D])/8. In particular this limit is not β/4, the target's normalized residual adjoint. Moreover any function weight whose associated residual probability is dV would have ρβ²=dV, hence ρ=1/4 almost everywhere; this likewise gives β/4 rather than the approximating-current limit.

5. Density regularity and loss of mass. For each δ>0 define F_δ^g=log((Ω_δ^g)²/(4dV)). It is smooth and bounded for that δ and satisfies the displayed smooth solution equation (Ω_δ^g)²=4e^{F_δ^g}dV. The C^∞ convergence of forms off D proves F_δ^g→0 in C^∞ there.

The lower positivity Ω_δ^g≥ω implies (Ω_δ^g)²≥ω²=2dV, so F_δ^g≥−log 2. In the explicit square formula above, a and K are bounded, λ,μ∈[0,1], and λμH≤(1−r)/(4r). Thus on X\D,
(Ω_δ^g)²/(4dV)≤C_g(1+1/r),
with C_g independent of δ. Combining upper and lower bounds gives |F_δ^g|≤C'_g+|log r|, and therefore also the claimed weaker estimate C''_g+2|log r|. All finite powers of |log r| are integrable: on the first factor this is ∫₀¹|log r|^pdr<∞. Dominated convergence consequently proves F_δ^g→0 in every finite L^p(dV).

On the other hand, ∫e^{F_δ^g}dV=(1/4)∫(Ω_δ^g)²=2 for every δ. The exponentials converge pointwise to 1 off D, which is a set of full smooth volume. They cannot converge to 1 in L¹. They also cannot be uniformly integrable: convergence almost everywhere together with uniform integrability on this probability space would force L¹ convergence and convergence of their integrals to 1. Equivalently, the computed limiting mass has an additional divisorial component. The smooth θ-class mass is 8, while the target non-pluripolar mass is only 4.

6. The logical obstruction and its boundary. The target has the admissible singular reference, smooth limiting density, ordinary-type solvability, and singleton support demanded by (U). Every approximation above is smooth and strictly positive, uniformly bounded below by the same Kähler form, and converges monotonically to exactly the same canonical target, in L¹, in the stated capacity, and smoothly off its poles. Nevertheless its normalized classical adjoint probabilities do not converge to the singleton support, and two choices of g give different probability limits. Its limiting adjoint current is not a locally integrable function-weighted non-pluripolar residual. These facts directly falsify the stated unrestricted implication.

The approximants are bounded and therefore are not individually of type φ; their smooth logarithmic densities are not uniformly bounded as δ→0. This proof concerns exactly the unrestricted smooth approximation class in (U). It does not establish failure for singularity-type-preserving approximations, normalization after removing divisorial concentration, relative-mass-preserving approximations, uniformly bounded logarithmic densities, or uniformly integrable exponentials. It supplies an obstruction, not an extension theorem for those narrower classes.

premises: Let U be a domain in C^m and H an analytic hypersurface in U. If q is plurisubharmonic on U\H and locally bounded above near H, its extension to H by limsup from U\H is plurisubharmonic on U and is the unique extension with the canonical upper representative. If q is locally bounded both above and below near H, this extension is locally bounded.

On a connected compact Riemannian manifold M without boundary, with Laplacian Delta=div grad and Riemannian volume dmu, there is a Green kernel G satisfying Delta_y G(x,y)=delta_x-1/Vol(M). Its additive constant can be chosen so that G<=0 and sup_x integral_M |G(x,y)|dmu(y)<infinity. For every smooth real f, f(x)-Vol(M)^(-1)integral_M f dmu=integral_M G(x,y)Delta f(y)dmu(y). On a compact Kähler manifold, the positivity-preserving Laplacian heat semigroup commutes with Delta and converges pointwise to the canonical representative of every bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic function; in particular a distributional lower bound Delta f>=-A is preserved by this regularization.

Let X be a compact Kähler surface, alpha a smooth closed Kähler form, and w a bounded canonical alpha-plurisubharmonic function. Put T=alpha+dd^c w and use bounded Bedford–Taylor products. Then T^2 and its mixed products with smooth closed semipositive forms are positive, T^2-alpha^2=dd^c(w(T+alpha)), and integral_X T^2=integral_X alpha^2. For every bounded canonical quasi-plurisubharmonic f, the signed mixed product dd^c f wedge (T+alpha) is defined and integral_X f(T^2-alpha^2)=integral_X w dd^c f wedge (T+alpha). If dd^c f>=-eta for a smooth closed semipositive form eta, this mixed product is bounded below by -eta wedge (T+alpha), and integral_X eta wedge T=integral_X eta wedge alpha.
